name: Metabase
description: Open source business intelligence and analytics platform. Create dashboards and explore data without writing SQL.
summary: Metabase is actively releasing updates across multiple version branches simultaneously. The latest stable release is v0.63.18 (released 16 Sep 2024), with a beta of v0.64.0 released on 24 Sep 2024. The project maintains several older branches in parallel (v0.58.x, v0.59.x, v0.60.x, v0.61.x, v0.62.x, v0.63.x), all receiving patch updates. Both Open Source and Enterprise editions are available via Docker and JAR downloads from https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Open Source edition uses AGPL v3; Enterprise edition uses a commercial license.
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases across several version branches in September 2024 alone.
answers.Is there a cloud-hosted version availabl: Yes — Metabase offers a managed cloud (Metabase Cloud) at metabase.com.
answers.Does it support SSO and SAML authenticat: Yes — SSO and SAML are supported in the Enterprise edition.
answers.What databases/data sources are supporte: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, MongoDB, SQLite, Oracle, Presto, Druid, SparkSQL, and more via drivers. Full list at metabase.com/docs.

alternatives.name: Redash
alternatives.review: Open source, query-focused, simpler feature set.

alternatives.name: Apache Superset
alternatives.review: Apache-licensed, rich visualisation library, steeper setup curve.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.review: Primarily metrics/time-series but increasingly used for general BI.

alternatives.name: Hex
alternatives.review: Close source, enterprise focus, AI Analytics Platform for your whole team

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.review: Tableau offers more advanced visualizations and enterprise features but is significantly more expensive and not open source unlike Metabase.

alternatives.name: Lightdash
alternatives.review: Lightdash integrates tightly with dbt for a metrics-layer-first approach, making it more structured for dbt users but less flexible for teams without dbt pipelines.
